newsitem.title: PERU: Peru captures rebels, frees German hostage-report.
newsitem.headline: Peru captures rebels, frees German hostage-report.

text.p: Peruvian security forces have captured five Marxist Tupac Amaru guerrillas and freed a German businessman they kidnapped in the eastern jungle zone, the daily Expreso reported on Saturday.
A policeman posing as a cousin of hostage Francisco Brack Egg set up the sting, which trapped the rebels as they were demanding a $30,000 ransom, the newspaper said.

Police could not immediately confirm the captures, which reportedly took place in the Chanchamayo coffee-growing region of Junin in the heart of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement's (MRTA) strongest zone.
The MRTA, which gained world notoriety during the four- month Lima hostage crisis, has an estimated 200 fighters in that area and has traditionally relied on kidnapping as a form of fund raising.
Fourteen MRTA rebels held 72 hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima for 126 days before Peruvian troops' dramatic April 22 rescue operation.

Expreso also reported that anti-terrorist police had arrested 84 suspects in Lima for their part in last Thursday's car-bomb attack by the larger Maoist guerrilla movement Shining Path. About 1,200 soldiers and 100 policemen made the arrests during a sweep of shantytowns.
Police spokesmen would not confirm the report.

Security forces throughout Peru were on maximum alert on Saturday in case of further attacks by Shining Path, marking the 17th anniversary of the May 17, 1980, start to its armed uprising. But there were no reports of attacks by late afternoon.
At least eight policemen and several civilians were injured in Thursday's powerful blast that destroyed a police station and did an estimated $600,000 damage to surrounding municipal buildings.
Violence by Shining Path and the MRTA has cost Peru at least 30,000 lives and $25 billion in infrastructure damage since 1980.
